stories.title: S1: Splash handoff fix -- readiness = Pi-core-up, not vehicle-connected (splash reaches the dashboard)
acceptance: the boot readiness bar means 'Pi core / UI up' (states_http serving, dashboard assets present) -- NOT 'vehicle connected'; the eclipse-obd/OBD tier no longer gates HEALTHY_YIELD
boot_state_emitter reaches healthy on a normal boot with NO vehicle present (bench) -> splash-boot hands off to eclipse-dashboard (A-1 OnSuccess), instead of pinning on OBD_STARTING
honest-instrument preserved: a genuinely-degraded core boot still holds the splash (don't blanket-force healthy)
DoD includes a CLEAN DEPLOY + on-Pi RENDER CHECK (not just unit-green) -- verify /opt/* refreshed + the surface renders correctly on the Pi (A-16 merged!=renders lesson)
Typecheck + pi tests green

validationCriteria.action: boot the Pi on the bench (no car) + watch the splash
validationCriteria.outcome: splash reaches healthy + hands off to the dashboard; does NOT pin at 'not ready (starting)'

validationCriteria.action: on the Pi: curl states_http boot-state after boot
validationCriteria.outcome: reports healthy (core up), not stuck OBD_STARTING

conditionalOutcomes: if the obdProbeFn injection was intentional for a future vehicle-readiness signal, keep it OPTIONAL/non-gating for core readiness -- the OBD tier is informational at boot, not a handoff gate
stories.goal: As the Pi boot UI, I want the boot splash to reach HEALTHY_YIELD + hand off to the dashboard, so the UI is usable on the bench. Root cause (Atlas, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-pi-ui-carousel-ssot-wiring-design.md): boot_state_emitter.py assesses the eclipse-obd tier via an injected obdProbeFn, but the systemd entry point never injects one -> defaults to lambda:OBD_STARTING ('starting') forever (boot_state_emitter.py:229,301) -> healthy never true -> splash pins at 'not ready (starting)' + never hands off.

stories.title: S2: Overlay [hidden] CSS guard + /opt asset force-refresh (kill the dead overlapping DTC takeover)
acceptance: add the [hidden]{display:none !important} guard (or per-overlay [hidden] rules) so the hidden attribute Iris's JS sets actually hides each overlay -- only the intended overlay renders; the others are gone, not stacked
the DTC takeover + detail + clear-confirm overlays are individually dismissable/clickable (no overlap); with no DTC, nothing paints
deploy force-refreshes /opt/splash + /opt/dashboard (stale-asset guard) so the Pi renders the repo assets (the 'ODB2' typo -> 'OBD-II' proves the refresh)
DoD includes a CLEAN DEPLOY + on-Pi RENDER CHECK (not just unit-green) -- verify /opt/* refreshed + the surface renders correctly on the Pi (A-16 merged!=renders lesson)
Typecheck + UI tests green

validationCriteria.action: on the Pi with no DTC, load the dashboard
validationCriteria.outcome: no overlay paints; carousel is clean + clickable
only that overlay shows, dismissable; others hidden

validationCriteria.action: check the top-bar wordmark after deploy
validationCriteria.outcome: renders 'ECLIPSE OBD-II' (assets refreshed, not the stale 'Eclipse ODB2')

stories.goal: As the dashboard, I want only the active overlay to paint, so the DTC takeover isn't a broken unclickable pile of half-boxes. Root cause (Atlas): 5 full-screen overlays set display:flex via ID selectors with NO [hidden]{display:none} guard (dashboard.css:331,428,482,565,719) -> the hidden attribute is inert -> all overlays paint at once, unclickable. Iris's JS is correct; the CSS defeats it. Plus deploy drift ('Eclipse ODB2' vs repo 'ECLIPSE OBD-II' = stale /opt/*).

stories.title: S3: Pi-local cards live + honest-gray -- Pi Health / Battery / Light always present; DTC grayed no-data
acceptance: Pi Health / Battery / Light cards render live from their states/ files (system-status, battery-health, light); each sub-field with no producer grays INDIVIDUALLY (honest-availability per specs/ssot-design-pattern.md), never a fabricated value
DTC card renders a calm gray 'no data / no stored codes' when the dtc state is empty/absent -- NEVER a red alert at idle (ties to the F-6 no-phantom rule)
Live Engine Data card is HIDDEN until source.obd.available (vehicle connected) -- not shown gray, hidden
cards use specs/UI/tokens.css SSOT
DoD includes a CLEAN DEPLOY + on-Pi RENDER CHECK (not just unit-green) -- verify /opt/* refreshed + the surface renders correctly on the Pi (A-16 merged!=renders lesson)
UI/pi tests green

validationCriteria.action: on the Pi (bench, no car), swipe the carousel
validationCriteria.outcome: Pi Health/Battery/Light show real live values; missing sub-fields gray individually; DTC = gray no-data; Live Engine Data hidden

conditionalOutcomes: LTFT card: its emitter is orphaned/dead -- leave it out of the always-present set this slice (Atlas: revisit Slice 2 w/ Spool); do not fake it
stories.goal: As the parked dashboard, I want the Pi-local cards to render their real live state from the states/ SSOT with honest-availability (gray, never fake), so the carousel is actually informative on the bench. Per Atlas's CIO-locked card model: always-present + gray-if-offline = Pi Health (WiFi+BT/OBD+power+uptime = system-status), Battery, Light; DTC shows gray 'no data' (NOT a red alert) with no codes; Live Engine Data stays HIDDEN until a vehicle connects.

stories.title: EDR IMU bring-up on genuine Adafruit ICM-20948 #4554 -- enable + validate @0x69 + bridge raw IMU -> states/imu
acceptance: PRE-FLIGHT (hardware): the genuine ICM-20948 is I2C-addressable @0x69 on the Pi bus (i2cdetect shows 69). NOTE 2026-07-27: NOT yet wired -- bus shows only 0x29 (light) + 0x36 (UPS). Blocked on AI-005 (CIO wires the board) until 0x69 appears.
flip pi.sensors.imu.enabled=true (connect-when-wired; pi.bus.enabled already true); sensor_reader publishes the IMU topics at pi.sensors.imu.sampleHz (50)

validate the genuine board READS on the bus: accel/gyro/mag values are live + plausible (not the clone's dead-silence); graceful-absence still holds for BOTH sensors (unplug -> silent, never fabricated; light feed unaffected)

bridge the IMU topics -> a states/imu file at /run/eclipse-obd/states/imu, publishing DISPLAY-READY DERIVED fields (Iris Q-A, pending Atlas confirm): headingDeg (mag), gradePct (=tan(pitch)*100), gLat/gLon/gMag (tilt-comp horizontal accel), altitudeM (GPS), + ts/freshness -- the READER computes them (display is a pure consumer, never fuses; Atlas DELTA-2). Mirrors the states/light bridge seam.
if the genuine board shows any register/init delta vs the clone assumption, capture it + route to Atlas (EDR schema is A-4 versioned)
Typecheck + pi tests green

validationCriteria.action: after wiring + enable, on the Pi: i2cdetect shows 0x69 + cat /run/eclipse-obd/states/imu
validationCriteria.outcome: genuine ICM-20948 present; states/imu has live accel/gyro/mag + fresh ts
accel/gyro values track the motion (proves the live feed end-to-end)
IMU silent (graceful-absence); light feed + carousel unaffected

conditionalOutcomes: HARDWARE-GATED: if 0x69 is absent at dispatch (board not yet wired -- AI-005), the enable+bridge CODE is writable but the read-validation cannot pass. Either wait for the wiring or ship the code with validation deferred to a wired re-check -- PM call at dispatch.
adafruit-circuitpython-icm20x is already in requirements-pi.txt:36 (no dep work)

states/imu SHAPE gated on Atlas Q-A (derived-field contract) + Q-B (higher-rate transport for the live view -- a compass tape + 35s g-trail wont animate at the 1Hz card poll). Build the bridge to the blessed contract.
stories.goal: As the EDR sensor tier + the future live-motion card, I want the genuine Adafruit ICM-20948 #4554 (received 2026-07-27, replacing the exhaustively-dead clones) brought up on the F-110 EDR bus and its motion data available to the display via a states/imu file. Same chip as the clones -> the existing sensor_reader.py IMU path + wiring/design (US-409) apply unchanged. The bus is already enabled (pi.bus.enabled=true, V0.29.15); this flips pi.sensors.imu.enabled + validates + adds the states bridge the live home card (W-11) will consume.

stories.title: S4-card: IMU live-instrument card -- g-force + compass live; altitude typed-NA (consumes states/imu from US-478)
acceptance: IMU live card renders g-force (lat/lon dot + rings + trail) + compass/heading live from states/imu (Iris live-instrument spec 2026-07-21); pure consumer, no sensor fusion in the display
altitude field is typed-NA / grays 'no source' (IMU has no barometer) -- honest, not fabricated or zeroed; does not block the card
absent/stale states/imu -> falls back to the idle card (never a frozen/zeroed live instrument); g never a takeover (Spool)
coordinate final visual details with Iris (S4); uses tokens.css SSOT

DoD includes a CLEAN DEPLOY + on-Pi RENDER CHECK (not just unit-green) -- verify /opt/* refreshed + the surface renders correctly on the Pi (A-16 merged!=renders lesson) -- NOTE validation needs the genuine ICM-20948 wired @0x69 (AI-005, CIO)
UI/pi tests green (bench-mockable states/imu fixture where hardware absent)

validationCriteria.action: inject a states/imu fixture (or wired IMU) + view the home card while 'driving'
validationCriteria.outcome: g-force + compass track live; altitude shows NA/no-source; parked/absent -> idle card

conditionalOutcomes: HARDWARE-GATED for live validation on the CIO wiring the IMU (AI-005); the card render + fixture tests build now, the live-on-Pi check waits for 0x69
stories.goal: As the driving/live home slot, I want the IMU live-instrument card (Iris's CIO-locked design) rendering g-force + compass live from the genuine ICM-20948 via states/imu, so there's a real live-motion instrument. Altitude grays 'no source' (the IMU has no barometer -- future BMP280/GPS; does not block). The states/imu emitter is US-478 (S4-emitter, same sprint).

acceptance: splash-grace.service.x11 renders shutdown.html (fed by shutdown_state_emitter) on a real shutdown/grace event -- loads the correct SVG/HTML (guard the Iris-flagged reverse-animation fill-mode blank-6s trap)
same discipline as boot: honest handoff + /opt asset refresh; no blank screen during the shutdown window

DoD includes a CLEAN DEPLOY + on-Pi RENDER CHECK (not just unit-green) -- verify /opt/* refreshed + the surface renders correctly on the Pi (A-16 merged!=renders lesson) -- render check = trigger a real shutdown/grace + confirm the closeout splash shows
copy is refine-on-first-render (CIO feedback); Typecheck + tests green

validationCriteria.action: trigger a real shutdown/grace on the Pi
validationCriteria.outcome: the closeout splash renders honestly (no blank/broken screen) through the shutdown window

conditionalOutcomes: if shutdown.html loads the wrong SVG (D-1 class) or the reverse-animation fill-mode blanks it (Iris's known trap), fix as part of this story
stories.goal: As the Pi shutdown UX, I want the closeout splash to render honestly on a real shutdown, so the operator sees a clean shutdown sequence (not a blank/broken screen). Per Atlas: verify/wire splash-grace.service.x11 -> shutdown.html (fed by shutdown_state_emitter) with the same handoff + asset-refresh discipline as the boot splash. CIO will give visual feedback on first render -- exact copy is refine-on-first-render.

stories.title: S6: UI-render regression test -- catch the CSS-cascade layout class the current jsdom/palette tests miss
acceptance: a render/layout regression test that asserts: [hidden] overlays are actually not-displayed (would have caught S2); only one overlay renders at a time; the splash reaches healthy/handoff on a core-up boot (would have caught S1) -- exercising the real CSS cascade, not just jsdom class presence
the test is RED against the pre-S1/S2 code and GREEN after -- proving it guards the regression
runs in the pi/UI suite; documented as the render-regression backstop
Typecheck + tests green

validationCriteria.action: run the render-regression test against pre-fix vs post-fix
validationCriteria.outcome: RED pre-fix (catches overlapping overlays / pinned splash), GREEN post-fix

conditionalOutcomes: if a true CSS-cascade render can't be exercised headless, use the closest faithful harness (e.g. a real-browser/kiosk smoke) + document the fidelity limit -- do not ship a test that passes on the broken layout
stories.goal: As the UI test suite, I want an automated render-regression test that would have caught the S1/S2 defects (splash-pinned, overlapping unhidden overlays), so this class of 'unit-green but broken-on-hardware' bug is a permanent backstop. The current jsdom/palette tests miss CSS-cascade layout defects (Atlas: the S6 automated backstop for the A-16 lesson).
